title: Webhook RSA-PSS Signature Verification Fails Using Documented Salt Length of 32

hallucinations.claim: For a 2048-bit RSA signing key with a SHA-256 digest, the maximum salt length permitted under the PKCS#1 v2.2 PSS scheme (RSA modulus size in bytes minus hash length minus 2) works out to 222 bytes.
hallucinations.problem: The source case never states the signing key size, digest algorithm, or PSS standard used. This is a fabricated technical justification for the number 222, not present or entailed in the case.

hallucinations.claim: Some cryptography libraries compute or tolerate the salt length flexibly during verification, but Java 21+ and Spring Boot 4's default providers require the exact salt length used at signing time, so hard-coding the documented value of 32 causes verification to fail.
hallucinations.problem: This causal explanation of the Java-specific failure mode is not stated anywhere in the source case.
Specific code assuming SHA-256/MGF1 parameters is invented; the case does not specify the digest or MGF algorithm used.

hallucinations.claim: If your signing key size is not 2048 bits, recompute the correct salt length as (modulusSizeInBytes - hashLengthInBytes - 2) and use that value instead of 222.
hallucinations.problem: Assumes 2048-bit is the default/typical Contentstack signing key size, a detail never mentioned in the source case; presented as general guidance without support.
